item.text:
**5B.4 Research Note**

**Verdict:** mostly positive, but narrower than a full pro-competition reform program. Srettha’s 2024 record shows real effort to open trade and investment channels, clarify business rules, and loosen some property-market restrictions. What I did not find was a broad anti-cartel, anti-rent-seeking overhaul or a clean property-rights package that clearly favored domestic entrepreneurs over politically connected actors.

**Positive**
- [World Bank Outlines Five Reform Priorities for Thailand to Revitalize Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/03/25/world-bank-outlines-five-reform-priorities-for-thailand-to-revitalize-growth) | World Bank | March 25, 2024 | The World Bank’s 2024 Thailand reform agenda explicitly called for a more competitive and innovative economy, stronger competition regulations, support for SMEs, and stronger fiscal institutions. This is strong evidence for fairer rules for entrepreneurship and investment. | QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.1, 5B.3

- [Thailand, Sri Lanka sign free trade agreement](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailand-sri-lanka-sign-free-trade-agreement-3291876) | Reuters via Investing.com | February 3, 2024 | Reuters reported that Srettha signed an FTA covering trade in goods, investment, customs procedure, and intellectual property rights, and urged private sectors to expand two-way trade and investment. This is direct evidence for pro-trade, pro-investment rulemaking. | QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.1

- [Thailand and Australia agree to boost Trade & Tourism cooperation](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/2078/iid/266801) | Public Relations Department, Thailand | March 6, 2024 | Thailand and Australia agreed to expand cooperation in trade, investment, tourism, technology, and innovation, and to improve the Thailand-Australia FTA. This supports a fairer, more open commercial environment for firms and job creation. | QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.1

- [Thailand sees at least $22 billion investment pledges in 2024](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thailand-sees-at-least-22-billion-investment-pledges-in-2024-3484417) | Reuters via Investing.com | June 14, 2024 | Reuters said the government expected at least 800 billion baht in investment applications, with Q1 applications up 31 percent year on year. This is positive evidence that the administration was attracting productive investment rather than deterring it. | QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.1, 5B.3

- [SEC releases a statement outlining guidelines for foreign business operators on providing investment services to Thai investors, and Ease of Doing Business guidelines to support Thailand as financial hub](https://www.sec.or.th/EN/Pages/News_Detail.aspx?SECID=11152&rand=113627) | Securities and Exchange Commission of Thailand | September 18, 2024 | The SEC clarified legal channels and scope for foreign business operators and framed the move as part of an ease-of-doing-business push for a financial hub. This is direct evidence of rule clarification and regulatory predictability. | QIDs: 5B.4

- [Thailand to Extend Duration of Foreign Land Leases and Condo Ownership](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/52/iid/300660) | Public Relations Department, Thailand | June 25, 2024 | The administration tasked Interior Ministry officials with amending laws to extend foreign land leases to 99 years and raise foreign condominium ownership to 75 percent, framing it as economic stimulus. This is positive for investment and property-rights openness, though still politically sensitive. | QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.1

**Caveats / negative side**
- [Pros and cons of expanding foreign rights to property ownership](https://www.nationthailand.com/business/property/40039924) | Nation Thailand | July 23, 2024 | Real-estate entrepreneurs argued that any liberalization needed strict anti-nominee and location safeguards, which signals that the reform was not yet obviously fair or complete. This is indirect negative evidence because it shows the policy needed guardrails to avoid distortion and abuse. | QIDs: 5B.4

- [Longer property leases for foreigners to boost slumping market: REIC](https://www.nationthailand.com/business/property/40039922) | Nation Thailand | July 23, 2024 | REIC backed looser foreign ownership rules but warned they had to be carefully regulated to avoid long-term harms. That is mixed evidence: pro-investment intent, but unresolved fairness and market-impact concerns. | QIDs: 5B.4

**Search gap**
- I found no direct 2024 evidence of a sweeping Srettha-led overhaul of competition law, anti-monopoly enforcement, or domestic property-rights reform for Thai entrepreneurs. The clearest evidence is concentrated in trade deals, investment promotion, financial-hub regulation, and selective real-estate liberalization.
